confidence_notes: I did four web searches out of the six allowed. One found the RBA USD/AUD rate for 2026-11-18: 0.6720 USD per AUD. I saw that figure in search results, including an aggregator, rather than reading the rba.gov.au page myself, so please check it against the official RBA page linked in source_url. The other three searches looked for Tottori food and drink prices. They found a CityCost cappuccino price of about ¥575, a Japan-wide Numbeo inexpensive meal of about ¥1,000 and mid-range meal for two of about ¥5,000, an automated travel-cost estimate of about $3.92 for a beer in Tottori, a general Japan guide figure of about ¥700 for a cocktail, and only a bottle price for wine, about ¥1,178. Tottori-specific data was thin and the dates were unclear. I could not find a direct Tottori price for a glass of wine or a cocktail. Those two anchors are based on the beer price and normal local izakaya and bar pricing, so they are less certain. Yen prices were converted at an assumed rate of about ¥150–160 per USD, which adds some uncertainty to every anchor. The accommodation anchors come only from my general knowledge, with no searches or listings checked. Tottori has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel figures are the least certain. Room prices assume July, which is summer travel season around the Tottori Sand Dunes.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tottori city is a small regional prefectural capital on the San'in coast. Its prices should be like other smaller Japanese regional cities such as Matsue, Yonago or Kochi. Restaurant and drink prices are a little below Japan's national averages and clearly below Tokyo; the CityCost data puts mid-range wine about 22% below Tokyo. Rooms are mostly business hotels with fairly low rates.
